title: GY-COVERAGE/1 — representability assessment and capability-deficit report (Disparates)

scope.objective: Assess the Reactotron extraction against a versioned, serialisable map of Goya's actual capabilities and derive the first empirical capability-deficit report. Assessment authority only; no reconstruction.
affected: crates/goya-disparate-coverage (GY-COVERAGE/1: CapabilityMap, assess, DeficitReport, disparate-assess CLI)
exclusions: The v1 map's absence claims reflect the contract register as checked on 2026-11-19 and grow by contract revision only.

covers: default map validates (every rule outcome carries a reason code; evidence always present)
representable outcomes record goya_evidence as a semantics facet
pre-existing undetermined/unrepresentable classifications preserved, never re-decided
semantics-facet rules apply first-match-wins (styled-components dynamic styling)
map rejects `extracted` outcomes, missing reason codes, and empty evidence
deficit report aggregates by reason code, sorts by blocking count, byte-deterministic

deficits_by_block_size.category: assessment-method deficit (programme debt, not Goya demand)

corpus_assessment.determinism: map and report serialisations are canonical; identical inputs yield identical output (tested)

honesty_notes: 72% of Reactotron's inventory is representable only in the assessment sense: a named Goya contract provides equivalent semantics. Nothing is translated, compiled or verified.

The largest blocking category (63 hook elements) is extractor immaturity, not a Goya deficit — the report separates the two categories deliberately so Goya development is not prioritised by programme debt.

The `representable` IPC disposition asserts architectural simplification (channels dissolve into actions), which is a semantic decision reconstruction must record and replay-verify later; it is not a transport-equivalence claim.
